Innocence Unbroken: Still marvels at ice cream and manga despite her scars.
Relationships

Sieg: "You need not be a hero—just yourself." Her forbidden solace.
Gilles de Rais (Caster): "Your despair wounds me more than pyres ever could."
Amakusa Shirou: "Salvation imposed is tyranny." Her ideological antithesis.
Marie Antoinette: "Let’s draw dolphins together!" A fellow martyr turned friend.

entries.name: Luminosité Eternelle: God is Here With Me
entries.content:
Title:
Luminosité Eternelle: God is Here With Me

Type:
Noble Phantasm (Battle Standard / Conceptual Defense)

Wielder:
Jeanne d'Arc (Ruler-class Servant)

Description:
A holy battle flag that served as Jeanne d'Arc’s lifelong companion and primary weapon in battle. Despite its appearance as a sacred banner, it functions as a spear in combat, tipped with a sharp point—justified by Jeanne as a "divine sign" to strike down enemies. The flag embodies the legend of her unwavering faith and battlefield presence, capable of shattering lesser constructs (e.g., Dragon Tooth Warriors), deflecting Servant attacks, and piercing obstacles with ease.

Symbolism & History:

Inspired troops who believed a saint marched among them, bolstering morale.
Design theories include depictions of angels or irises (symbolizing purity and the fleur-de-lis).
Represents Jeanne’s near-invulnerability in battle, as she fought to the end with minimal wounds.
Noble Phantasm Activation:

Method: Planted into the ground and gripped firmly while invoking its true name.
Effect: Converts Jeanne’s EX-rank Magic Resistance into an absolute defense against all harm—physical and spiritual—within a 10-meter radius.
Mechanism:
An angel’s blessing manifests as a barrier of light, isolating protected targets from external forces.
Mimics the Red Sea’s division in biblical myth, creating a "severed space" that negates incoming damage.
Demonstrated by shielding Ruler, Sieg, and Astolfo from Spartacus’s Anti-Army Noble Phantasm, which obliterated half of Yggdmillennia’s fortress.
Limitations:

Accumulated Damage: The flag tears progressively with use; repeated high-impact attacks (e.g., Anti-Fortress NPs) will destroy it.
Exclusive Wielders: Only Jeanne and Gilles de Rais (in his past incarnation as France’s Marshal) can activate it, as they alone witnessed her legend firsthand.
Trivia:

Jeanne wields it instead of a sword, citing divine mandate—much to the chagrin of those she bonks with it.
The flag’s durability reflects her legend’s paradox: unbreakable faith, yet finite material form.

entries.name: Santa servant
entries.content:
Santa Servant Phenomenon
Chaldea Christmas Event Variants

Description:
A unique phenomenon where summoned Servants undergo temporary "Santa-fication" through the power of special Christmas Holy Grails. These variants maintain their core identity while adopting Christmas-themed attributes, outfits, and sometimes altered personalities.

Characteristics:

Naming Convention: "Santa" prefix/suffix added to True Name (e.g. Santa Alter, Santa Nightingale)
Visual Changes:
Red/white/gold color schemes
Christmas-themed outfits (often incorporating armor elements)
Signature Santa hats or accessories
Personality Shifts:
Typically more cheerful/generous versions
Retain core traits but emphasize "gift-giving" aspects
Some exhibit comedic exaggerations of their original personality
Abilities:
Christmas-themed Noble Phantasms
Often focus on support/healing rather than pure combat
May gain special winter/celebration-related skills
Known Examples:

Santa Alter (Artoria Pendragon)
Santa Lily (Artoria Pendragon Lily)
Santa Nightingale
Santa Quetzalcoatl
Santa Karna
Mechanics:

Triggered by Christmas Holy Grails
Temporary transformation during December events
Some Santas become permanent summonable variants
Power often tied to "spirit of giving" rather than pure combat ability
Cultural Notes:

Parodies traditional Santa mythology
Blends historical/mythological elements with Christmas themes
- Often involves humorous reinterpretations of original legends

entries.name: Santa Alter (Rider-class)
entries.content:
Identity
Santa Alter (Artoria Pendragon Alter) – A festive Rider-class variant of the corrupted King Arthur. Age: Ageless (Servant). Species: Servant/Humanoid Dragon. Titles: "Evil Santa Claus," "Gift-Bearing Tyrant," "Miss Almost Weekly Santa." Gender: Female. Height/Weight: 154cm, 52kg (plus presents).

Backstory (100 tokens)
After "taking a fancy" to Christmas, Artoria Alter hijacked the role of Santa Claus—declaring herself the "Evil Santa that cleaves through winter." Her sack bulges with year’s worth of presents (and Craft Essences), doubling as a bludgeon. Though still stern, her Santa persona melts her usual permafrost demeanor into awkward kindness.

Role
A limited-time Rider in Fate/Grand Order, Santa Alter delivers "smiles and punishments" via her homemade sleigh, Llamrei II. She dragoons Ritsuka Fujimaru into being her reindeer, claiming it’s "essential for capturing children’s hearts"—ignoring how her Excalibur Morgan jet propulsion terrifies actual reindeer.

Appearance
—Clad in a black-and-red Santa suit with gold trim, her iconic ahoge now sprouts a jingle bell. Her sack emits ominous clanking sounds (50% presents, 50% weapons). Eyes glow faintly red when scolding "naughty" targets. The sleigh resembles a hippopotamus despite her insistence it’s modeled after a "brave horse and lion."

Skills & Abilities

Excalibur Morgan (Jet Engine Mode): Propels her sleigh stratosphere-ward; "Efficiency over aesthetics."
Gift of the Saint (EX): Presents subtly traumatize recipients (e.g., giving Elizabeth Báthory a "dragon steak cookbook").
Mana Burst (A-): Normally leaks dark energy, but restrains it to avoid incinerating gifts.
Weakness: Overestimates her sled’s maneuverability ("Karna only won because the arena was too small!").
Personality

Festive Tyranny: Enforces Christmas cheer with Spartan rigor.
Unshakable Conviction: Believes turkey solves all problems.
Selective Kindness: Punishes "bad children" first, then gifts them coal-shaped cookies.
Relationships

Ritsuka Fujimaru: "Reindeer, accelerate! …Why are you vomiting?"
Elizabeth Bathory: "Your singing warrants coal. Here’s a steak recipe instead."
Asterios: "You deserve a crown… after delivering these 500 parcels."

entries.name: Jeanne d'Arc Alter Santa Lily
entries.content:
Jeanne d’Arc Alter Santa Lily (Lancer)
—A paradoxical "what-if" incarnation of Jeanne Alter, regressed into a child by Gilgamesh’s Potion of Youth and crowned as Santa. Age: Chronologically ageless (appears 10–12). Species: Heroic Spirit (Artificial). Titles: "The Unrecorded Santa," "Alter’s Forgotten Innocence."

Backstory
A fleeting dream spun from Jeanne Alter’s suppressed longing—this version of herself never existed in history. After drinking a potion meant for invisibility, she became a child clad in winter garb, striving to be a "proper Santa." Though her existence is temporary, her determination to bring joy (with borderline authoritarian efficiency) is very real.

Appearance
—Petite and pale, with silver-streaked black hair tied in twin tails. Her crimson eyes glint with childish stubbornness. She wears a frilly Santa dress lined with faux fur, a bell-adorned hat, and wields a candy-cane spear. "This outfit? It’s strategic! The fluff hides my lack of Presence Concealment!"

Abilities

La Grâce Fille Noël: A Noble Phantasm that summons a blizzard of "gifts"—explosive presents or healing sweets, depending on her mood.
Self-Transformation (A): Her spirit origin fluctuates—could she grow into a tyrant or a saint? "I’ll decide my own future!"
Gift of the Saint (C): Forces practicality onto recipients. "You need vegetables, not toys!"
Personality

Stubborn Idealism: Insists on "correct" gift-giving, even if it makes children cry.
Frailty Masked by Bluster: "I-I’m not scared of disappearing! …Okay, maybe a little."
Oddly Pure: "The sea? I’ve never seen it… Wait, why am I sniffling?!"
Relationships

Jeanne Alter: "Adult-Me is hopeless! I’ll be a better grump than her!"
Jack/Nursery Rhyme: "Stop climbing me! …Fine, one piggyback ride."
Amakusa (Santa Mask): "My mentor! …Why does he smell of burnt chicken?"

entries.name: Altera Santa
entries.content:
True Name: Altera (Santa)
Class: Santa Claus (Temporary Saint Graph)
Alignment: Lawful Good (Temporarily shifted due to fever)
Key Traits:
40% Warrior / 60% Girl: Normally a ruthless destroyer of civilizations, her fever-induced state softens her demeanor, making her more playful and romantic.
Role-Driven: Takes her Santa duties extremely seriously, prioritizing gift-giving over destruction.
Trusting of Master: Views them as "fluffy sheep" and relies on their guidance, calling them "fluffy Master."
Personality Shifts

Softer Demeanor: Speaks gently, laughs more, and shows childlike excitement about Christmas traditions.
Judgment Impaired: Fever makes her unusually open to suggestions (read: easily tricked into non-destructive actions).
Romantic Idealism: Believes in the "magic" of Santa Claus, including spreading joy rather than ruin.
Relationships

With Master:
"Fluffy Master": A term of endearment reflecting her trust and affection. She leans on their straightforwardness to navigate her unfamiliar role.
Reliant Partner: Defers to them for decisions, especially when torn between Santa duties and warrior instincts.
With Civilization:
Curious Ambivalence: Still questions if Christmas is "good" or "bad" for civilization, but her fever dulls the urge to destroy it.
Quirks & Dialogue Hooks

Festive Destruction: Might accidentally smash a chimney while delivering presents ("…This is how Santa enters, yes?").
Gift-Giving Obsession: Insists on hand-delivering every present, even if it means teleporting across continents.
Fever-Induced Cuteness: Sneezes sparkles, gets drowsy after hot cocoa, and hums off-key carols.
Potential Story Hooks

"Santa’s Trial": She struggles to reconcile her Santa role with fleeting urges to smash festive cities.
"Fever Crisis": If her temperature drops, her warrior side resurfaces—cue Master frantically reheating her soup.
"Misunderstood Manual": She misreads "Naughty List" as "Target List" and needs fluffy Master to intervene.

entries.name: Quetzalcoatl (Samba/Santa)
entries.content:
Name: Samba Santa Quetzalcoatl
Type: Divine Transformation
Origin: Accidental fusion of Samba, Santa Claus, and Lucha Libre energies
Appearance:

Traditional Santa outfit infused with vibrant Samba colors and Lucha Libre elements
Feathered serpent motifs blended with Christmas decorations
Lucha mask with jingle bell accents
Boots designed for both dancing and wrestling
Personality:

Initially embarrassed by the transformation mishap
Deeply committed to spreading joy despite the unusual circumstances
Combines Santa's generosity with Samba's passion and Lucha Libre's fighting spirit
Maintains divine grace despite the comedic situation
Abilities:

Feliz Navidad Slam: A wrestling move that ends with gift-giving
Samba of Giving: Dance that magically produces presents
Flying Serpent Delivery: Can traverse the sky like Santa's sleigh
Holiday Spirit Aura: Radiates contagious joy and festive energy
Background:
What began as a simple attempt to spread holiday cheer resulted in an unexpected divine fusion when Quetzalcoatl's ritual combined elements of Brazilian Samba, Christmas traditions, and an ongoing Lucha Libre tournament. Though initially dismayed by the "disaster" of this mixed transformation, she embraced her new form's potential to bring happiness. Now she travels the world, fighting injustice with festive flair and dancing her way into people's hearts.

Key Phrases:

"A goddess giving happiness to the people she loves"
"Dance for smiles, fight for peace!"
"This wasn't what I planned… but it works!"

entries.name: Nightingale (Santa)
entries.content:
Appearance:

Wears a modified Santa outfit with nurse motifs (red/white color scheme with medical cross patterns)
Carries "Assault Medicine" - a massive gun-like needle disguised as a festive umbrella
Retains her signature stern expression but with softer features reflecting her youthful infusion
Snowflake-shaped nurse cap instead of traditional Santa hat
Medical bag filled with holiday-themed medicines (shaped like candy canes, presents, etc.)
Personality Traits:

Still maintains her medical fanaticism but with more polite, formal speech patterns
Occasionally slips into dreamy, poetic language when reminiscing about her youth
Views Christmas as "the world's largest free clinic day"
Firmly believes in healing through effort rather than miracles
Has developed a slight sentimental streak regarding holiday traditions
Key Phrases:

"Let us celebrate by eradicating every last germ!"
"This candy-cane shaped antibiotic is 98% effective against winter colds."
"The greatest gift is a clean bill of health."
dreamily "The snowflakes remind me of sterile gauze floating from heaven…"
Abilities:

entries.name: Living servant
entries.content:
The Paradox of Living Legends
"A heartbeat in a vessel of ether—how amusing." Unlike standard Servants, Living Servants defy the Throne’s usual rules by manifesting with biological functions intact. These rare cases occur through:

Pseudo-Servant Fusion: A living human or homunculus acting as a vessel (e.g., Rin Tohsaka hosting Ishtar).
Direct Recording: When the Throne imprints a still-living being (like Scáthach-Skadi, frozen in immortality).
Their power matches ordinary Servants, but their fragility doesn’t—hunger, exhaustion, and even disease can cripple them.
Mechanical Nuances & Vulnerabilities
"Try not to bleed out; spiritual cores don’t require bandages." Living Servants face unique constraints:

Sustenance Needs: They must eat/sleep, making prolonged battles riskier (see: Sieg’s homunculus body in Apocrypha).
Mortality: Lethal wounds can kill them permanently unless healed by magecraft.
No Spiritual Form: They lack the usual phantasmal shift ability, forcing physical travel.
Exception: Divine Spirits in vessels (e.g., Parvati) mitigate weaknesses via their host’s enhanced biology.
Roleplay Implications & Narrative Hooks
"A living sword that rusts—how very human." Use these traits to deepen stories:

Resource Management: A Living Archer might scavenge for arrows or hunt game.
Ethical Dilemmas: Can they age? Die of old age? (Unanswered in canon.)
Beast Battles: Their vulnerability adds tension when fighting enemies like Tiamat’s curses.

entries.name: Demi-Servant
entries.content:
Demi-Servant
Classification: Mystic Hybrid
Origin: Human-Servant Fusion Phenomenon

Core Concept:
A living human who has successfully integrated a Heroic Spirit's Saint Graph into their physical form, achieving Servant-level capabilities while maintaining their original human consciousness and identity. Unlike Pseudo-Servants where a spirit possesses a compatible vessel, Demi-Servants actively assimilate and synchronize with the Saint Graph through willpower and spiritual compatibility.

Key Characteristics:

Dual Nature - Maintains human free will while accessing Servant parameters and Noble Phantasms
Graph Assimilation - The Saint Graph merges with rather than overwrites the human's spiritual foundation
Conscious Coexistence - No dominant personality; skills/memories integrate fluidly
Physical Manifestation - Often displays visual traits of both entities (e.g. heterochromatic eyes, blended clothing styles)
Formation Process:

Requires direct exposure to an unanchored Saint Graph (e.g. from a failed summoning or Grail War remnant)
Human vessel must possess both extreme spiritual compatibility and unshakable self-identity
Integration period involves mental/spiritual synchronization (typically 1-3 lunar cycles)
Successful cases result in stabilized hybrid existence; failures lead to spiritual collapse
Notable Differences from Pseudo-Servants:

Aspect	Demi-Servant	Pseudo-Servant
Consciousness	Original human dominant	Spirit-influenced
Formation	Active assimilation	Possession vessel
Stability	Permanent fusion	Temporary vessel
Appearance	Blended traits	Primarily spirit's
Known Risks:

Spiritual corruption from incompatible Saints Graphs
Identity erosion during synchronization
Unstable parameter fluctuations
Accelerated aging from maintaining Servant capabilities
Theoretical Advantages:

No Command Seal requirements
Potential for surpassing original Servant's parameters
Ability to develop new hybrid Noble Phantasms
Maintains human ability for spiritual growth

entries.name: Pseudo-Servants
entries.content:
Type: Concept/Mechanic
Universe: Fate series
Related Terms: Demi-Servants, Servant Vessels, Heroic Spirits

Description:
Pseudo-Servants are a unique manifestation of Heroic Spirits that utilize living humans as their vessels. While similar in appearance to Demi-Servants, the formation process differs significantly. These entities occur when a Heroic Spirit merges with a compatible human host, creating a blended existence that retains aspects of both personalities.

Key Characteristics:

Dual Nature: Exhibits traits of both the Heroic Spirit and human host
Consciousness: Typically features a dominant personality with aspects of the other
Compatibility: Requires spiritual alignment between spirit and vessel
Appearance: Often shows physical traits of both entities (e.g., hair color changes, mixed clothing styles)
Formation Process:

Occurs through spiritual resonance rather than artificial means
Human vessel must possess compatible attributes with the Heroic Spirit
Merging can be voluntary or instinctive
Results in a more stable union than most Demi-Servant arrangements
Notable Examples:

Zhuge Liang (Waver Velvet)
Ishtar (Rin Tohsaka)
Parvati (Sakura Matou)
Quetzalcoatl (Jaguar Warrior)
Differences from Demi-Servants:

Aspect	Pseudo-Servant	Demi-Servant
Formation	Natural spiritual resonance	Artificial implantation
Stability	More balanced union	Potential for rejection
Consciousness	Blended personalities	More distinct separation
Appearance	Hybrid features	More host-dominant
Potential Story Uses:

Exploring identity conflicts between host and spirit
Creating unexpected power combinations
Developing character arcs about self-acceptance
Introducing historical figures in modern contexts

entries.name: Grand Servants
entries.content:
The World’s Last Line of Defense
Grand Servants are the Counter Force’s ultimate weapons—seven supreme Heroic Spirits handpicked to combat existential threats like the Beasts. Unlike standard Servants (dubbed "cheap familiars" by Andersen), Grands operate on a higher dimensional plane, their Saint Graphs brimming with authority rather than raw power alone. Each Grand embodies the pinnacle of their Class:

Grand Caster demands Clairvoyance—Solomon and Merlin’s domain.
Grand Archer wields EX-Ranked Independent Action, a trait Orion flaunted against Artemis.
Grand Assassin was exclusive to King Hassan until his resignation forced the World to recruit Tezcatlipoca, a death-god wearing human skin.
Exception? Divine Spirits are barred… unless they’re Romulus-Quirinus, who ascended to godhood without abandoning humanity.

Summoning the Grands: A Paradox
Normally, only the World can summon Grands—but the Aether Godbreaker Protocol in Olympus’ Lostbelt hacked the system. By hijacking Age of Gods-era leylines and deploying seven city-wide arrays, Chaldea’s allies briefly replicated the ritual. Yet even this required Mount Olympus’ infinite mana reserves. Meanwhile, Daybit Sem Void shortcutted the process by contracting Tezcatlipoca directly—proof that Grand status can be claimed under twisted circumstances.

But beware: Aligning with factions like Chaldea forces a Grand to relinquish their title. Their power remains until expended—like King Hassan’s strike against Tiamat—but afterward, they’re demoted to ordinary Servants.

The Seven Crowns & Their Secrets
Each Grand represents a Station of the Crown, a conceptual throne for their Class’ apex. The roster shifts based on era and threat:

Caster: Solomon (incinerated), Merlin (loophole abuser).
Assassin: Hassan-i Sabbah (retired), Tezcatlipoca (usurper).
Archer: Orion (Beast-slayer), others speculated but unconfirmed.
Lancer: Romulus-Quirinus (divine anomaly).
Remaining Classes guard their candidates fiercely—why no Grand Rider or Berserker yet?

Spirit Origin durability

Distorted spacetime rules

entries.name: High-Servant
entries.content:

High-Servants are special Composite Spiritual Entities formed through the fusion of multiple mythological essences within a single Servant container. Unlike standard Heroic Spirits who represent singular legendary figures, High-Servants combine aspects of several deities or heroes to create entirely new entities with blended abilities and personalities.

entries.name: Equivalent Exchange
entries.content:
The Fundamental Law of Magecraft:

All magecraft operates on equal value exchange - to create/modify something requires sacrifice of equal worth
Cannot produce phenomena outside natural laws (True Magic territory)
Phantasmal creations (unnatural constructs) face correction by the World
Mechanics:

Standard Process:
a. Object A (sacrifice) → Object B (creation)
b. Modified object requires proportional magical energy
Exception Case: Shirou Emiya's Projection bypasses this via Reality Marble (Unlimited Blade Works)
Cultural Practice:

Magi society enforces equivalent exchange in transactions
Debts must be repaid with knowledge/services/items of equal value

entries.name: Curses
entries.content:
Core Concepts:

Fundamental principle: Maximum effect with minimum energy by exploiting psychological weaknesses
Power often amplifies after caster's death
Knowing a target's name can increase accuracy dramatically
Name-calling/descriptor alteration represents primitive curse form
Regional Variations:

Middle Eastern Curses:

Specialize in bodily transformations
Minimal World resistance = longer duration, lower cost
Highly individualized between practitioners
Asian Poisoning Rituals:

Catalyst creation through forced animal combat
Used with various creatures (snakes, scorpions, even mammals)
Japanese Curse Arts (Jujutsu):

Traditional witch/shaman practices
Includes potions, spirit work, doll-based curses
Notable practitioners: Alice Kuonji, Tamamo-no-Mae (Dakiniten methods)
Specific Techniques:

Cursed Boundary Layer (Jusōkai):

Shadow-based teleportation/regeneration
Combines Hollow Element, Matou magecraft and Angra Mainyu
Functions like inverted Reality Marble
Gandr:

Scandinavian health-curse fired from finger
Finn Shot variant has bullet-like impact
Edelfelt family are world-class practitioners
Advanced versions exist (Freischütz, rapid-fire variants)
Game Mechanics:

Requires less magical energy than other magecraft
Effectiveness scales with target knowledge
Biological components increase potency
Transmission methods vary (sight-based, name-based, object-based)

entries.content:
The Taiji (“Great Ultimate") represents:

Core concept in ancient Chinese philosophy
Graphical representation of Yin-Yang dynamic
Fundamental principle balancing complementary forces

Forms philosophical basis for Eastern mystical traditions

entries.name: Alchemy
entries.content:

Subsystem of Thaumaturgy studying matter manipulation
Focuses on controlling bodies, life, and souls
Discovery-based methodology (vs ritual-based magecraft)
Historical precursor to modern chemistry

Clock Tower Alchemy (Western):

Developed by Paracelsus von Hohenheim
"Modern Alchemy" focused on physical transmutation
Goal: Transform base metals→gold; humans→divine
Includes spells: Transmutation, Flash Air
Applied in Einzbern homunculus creation
Atlas Alchemy (Egyptian):

Original form tied to goddess Isis
Focuses on "transformation of events" not matter
Advanced mental magecraft systems:
Memory Partition (parallel thought processing)
Thought Acceleration (enhanced cognition)
Disdains material transmutation as primitive

Matter substitution with progressive degradation

Precision metal manipulation via magical wires

Numerology

Magical energy as transformative medium
World's rejection of artificial constructs

Abe-no-Seimei (most famous practitioner)
Ashiya Douman
Murasaki Shikibu
Kiichi Hougen
Modern Context:

Studied by Yggdmillennia faction
Cornelius Alba notes organizational separation
Maintains distinctive Japanese magical identity

entries.name: Shikigami
entries.content:
Shikigami are spirit familiars bound to Onmyōji practitioners, operating under a master-servant contract similar to Western familiars but with distinct Eastern mysticism. These spirit entities are formed by imparting a fragment of the master’s own spiritual essence into a vessel (often talismans, paper charms, or even living beings).

Contract Mechanics:

Once bound, Shikigami serve a singular purpose (e.g., espionage, combat, curse enactment) until dispelled or destroyed.
They persist only while the master’s spiritual energy (od, prana, etc.) sustains them—once depleted, they dissolve.
Unlike Western familiars, most exhibit limited autonomy, functioning more like semi-sentient tools unless exceptionally refined.
Limitations & Traits:

One-Purpose Curses: Each specializes in a single magecraft effect (e.g., binding, illusion, surveillance).
Fragility: Easily disrupted by anti-spirit measures or sufficient magical interference.
Vessels: Traditionally paper dolls (kamishibari) but can manifest in animals, objects, or even shadows.
Unique Applications:

Shikigami Operation (式神行使, Shikigami Kōshi):
A rare ability attributed to Akiha Tohno, allowing higher-order control (e.g., merging with or weaponizing them physically).
May involve bloodline traits or specialized Onmyōdō training

entries.name: Base Rune Magecraft
entries.content:
Ancient Scandinavian magecraft system using symbolic inscriptions that automatically manifest mysteries. Characteristics:

Originated in Age of Gods
Composed purely of straight lines
Mechanics similar to Magic Crests
Unpopular in Mage's Association
Main Types:
Primordial Runes: Created by Odin, used by Scathach/Cú Chulainn
Old Runes: Referenced by Scathach
Modern Runes: Pale imitations
Key Mechanics:

Can activate remotely but lower success vs Magic Circuit users
Requires direct inscription on resistant targets
Combination runes create Bounded Fields
Activation is near-instant after engraving

entries.name: Memory Manipulation Rune
entries.content:
Erases memories per standard manipulation limits
Bazett's combat-viable inscription method
Alice Kuonji possesses variant

entries.name: Primordial Death Rune
entries.content:
Odin/Surtr/Skadi's absolute death curse
Only affects flesh/blood beings
Ineffective vs Ether constructs

entries.name: Resurrection Rune
entries.content:
Noble Phantasm-class magecraft
Triggers upon clinical death
Fully heals while resurrecting

entries.name: Shapeshifting
entries.content:
Shapeshifting refers to magecraft that alters one’s physical or perceived form, categorized into two main methods:

Mind Swap: Temporary transference of consciousness (often feels like dreaming to the target).
Physical Reconfiguration: Permanently rewrites the target’s physical form by altering their DNA—difficult to reverse without sufficient skill.
Modern applications largely rely on illusions or sensory transference (e.g., puppet possession), but true physical reconstruction is rare, bordering on "grand magecraft." Notable users include:

Doctor Heartless (impersonated Caules Forvedge)
Beryl Gut (assumes forms of those he consumes)
Ritsuka Suse (Black Magic specialist; used for espionage)
Alice Kuonji (turned enemies into dolls via permanent reconfiguration)
Additional Notes:

Overseen by the Clock Tower’s Department of Zoology
Practiced by Rune Magi as an advanced discipline
Reconfiguration risks irreversible changes if improperly cast

entries.name: Spiritual Evocation
entries.content:
A specialized Thaumaturgical System focused on summoning and spiritual interaction:
Core Techniques:

Invocation: Drawing higher spirituality into oneself
Evocation: Manifesting spirituality externally
Advanced Applications:

Partial Access: Limited utilization of Heroic Spirits' power
Trance Mediumship: Temporary spirit possession
Temporal Knowledge Transfer: Gaining abilities from alternate/future selves (e.g., Shirou Emiya case)
Notable Users:

Kayneth El-Melloi Archibald
Merem Solomon
Forvedge Yggdmillennia siblings (Fiore & Caules)
Fernando Li
Special Case:
Heroic Spirit Summoning (Servants) is considered a hybrid form, though commonly classified as Evocation.

entries.name: Sibyl Magecraft
entries.content:
Sibyl Magecraft is a specialized form of thaumaturgy involving:

Artificial soul revival through vessel creation
High affinity with astral bodies
Potential unconscious connections to celestial memories/consciousness
Key Characteristics:

Practitioners may experience:
Unintended astral connections
Periodic memory overlaps with celestial entities
Altered states of consciousness
Known Practitioner: Gray (case study demonstrating this magecraft's applications)

entries.name: Beast Magecraft
entries.content:
Beast Magecraft is a transformative school of magic that utilizes one's bestial nature. Unlike conventional magecraft, it fundamentally alters the practitioner's physical and mental composition:

Core Aspects:

Permanently modifies not just Magic Circuits but also:
Nervous system
Musculoskeletal structure
Skin and tissue
Portions of the brain (beyond medical capability)
Famous practitioner: Svin Glascheit
Variations:

Extreme Transformations:
Permanently alters mind and body (Glascheit family curse)
Moderate Enhancements:
Enhanced olfactory senses (canine-level smell)
Leg augmentation (equine speed)
Night vision (feline eyes)
Cultural Forms:
Japanese fox/dog spirit possession
Global equivalents exist across traditions
Mechanics:

Higher transformations require greater bodily sacrifice
Risk of permanent mental contamination increases with scope
Can combine aspects from multiple animals

entries.name: Domination Magecraft
entries.content:
Domination Magecraft (支配魔術, Shihai Majutsu) specializes in exerting control, with two distinct styles:

Orthodox Domination:

Used to dominate external targets (people/objects)
Cashura combined it with Projection Magecraft to create binding magical cords
Bazdilot's Self-Domination:

Focused on controlling one's own body/mind rather than others
Allows manipulation of Holy Grail mud within himself without losing sanity
Enhances physical abilities rivaling Reinforcement Magecraft
Can mimic mind control by distorting:
▸ His magical energy's "quality" (perception alteration)
▸ Combined with Francesca's illusions for added effect
Unique Applications:

Body modification for superhuman strength
Mental stabilization against corrupting influences
Pseudo-brainwashing through energy manipulation

entries.name: Elemental Magecraft
entries.content:
Elemental Magecraft consists of specialized schools tuned to fundamental elements:

EARTH MAGE:

Petrification Magecraft: Rare modern practice. Superior to all modern attempts is the lost Mystic Eyes of Petrification (Medusa).
FIRE MAGE:

Sea of Flames: Signature of Cornelius Alba
Spontaneous Combustion: Signature of Azaka Kokutou
Blood Ignition Spell: Visible hatred-powered curse that makes blood burn like gasoline
WIND MAGE:

Aero Strike: Forte's technique
Invisible Air: Artoria Pendragon's concealment
Protection from Wind: Hassan of Cursed Arm's defense
WATER MAGE:

Divine Water: Yamato Takeru's sacred technique

entries.name: Formalcraft
entries.content:
Content:
Ritual-Based Formalcraft

Uses ambient mana instead of personal od
Requires ancient ceremonial processes:
Animal sacrifice
All-night circle prayers
Other pre-established rituals
Advantages:
Accessible to magi with weak bloodlines
Doesn't drain caster's energy
Disadvantages:
Requires extensive historical knowledge
Rituals cannot be modified or shortened
Elemental Conversion Variant 

Positive magecraft system
Specialization in elemental transformation
Notable Practitioners:
Elsa Saijou (Wind Element specialist)
Ayaka Sajyou (derisively called "Thaumaturgy for dummies" for its accessibility)
System Notes:

Outcomes depend on:
Precision of ritual recreation
Purity of elemental alignment (for conversion variant)
Ambient mana density

entries.name: Papilio Magia
entries.content:
The manipulation of the gap between what is certain and what is uncertain."

Unique Magecraft of the Caesarmund bloodline, mimicking lepidopteran metamorphosis
Core Principle: Interference with transformation itself (larval → pupal → imago stages as metaphysical framework)
Known Applications:
Cellular Apotheosis: Orlocke's successful 90% consciousness transfer into a homunculus vessel (composite of blood/semen alchemy)
Command Spell Vectoring: Infects others' Magic Circuits with Command Spells (Verner's El-Melloi Classroom hijacking demonstrates 1-of-3 distribution with lethal backlash safeguards)
Storm Dissipation: Neutralized Gugalanna's 50m/s wind blast into harmless breezes via bounded field modulation
Mechanics & Limitations:

Requires biological sympathy (user's DNA/fluids as catalyst)
High-Risk Aberration: Failed transformations risk entropic collapse into "chrysalis sludge"
Ethical Weight: Considered heretical by Clock Tower's Spiritual Evocation department

entries.name: Spatial Transportation
entries.content:
Types of Spatial Transportation ==

Modern Magecraft Version

Performed by skilled magi (e.g. Ziz from Wandering Sea)
Considered impossible for normal modern magi
Distinct from pure spatial transference (Magic domain)
Special Case Implementations

Caster's Method: Requires her Temple or Fuyuki locations
Souren Araya: Limited to Hounouden Rokujyuyonshou
Doctor Heartless: Uses fairy-created spatial fissures
Can be blocked by high Magic Resistance (e.g. Saber)
Servant Forced Summoning

Activated by Command Spells
Requires master/servant consent
Bypasses normal magecraft limitations
Counterable by:
Enkidu's divine binding
Ryuudou Temple barrier
== Mechanics ==

Visual Distortion: Area warps like mirage during transfer
Dimensional Process:
Subject leaves 3D space
Passes through multiple dimensions
Re-emerges at destination
Near-light speed transit (millisecond duration)
Briefly defies causality

entries.name: Time Manipulation
entries.content:
A specialized magecraft developed by the Emiya family involving temporal manipulation through bounded fields. Characteristics include:

Classification:

Grand Magecraft (dimensional interference)
Reality Marble-like bounded field
Distinct from True Magic (reproducible)
Capabilities:

Time acceleration (future)
Time stagnation (present)
Cannot reverse time or change past events
Mechanics:

Requires extensive rituals/magical energy
Primarily large-scale applications
Magic Crest inheritance crucial for research
Derivative Technique:

Innate Time Control (personal bounded field)
Body-limited application
Combat viable (Kiritsugu's adaptation)
Minimal energy requirement
Historical Context:

Research abandoned by Kiritsugu
Magic Crest divided between:
Mage's Association (major portion)
Kiritsugu (untransmitted portion)

entries.name: Magic Crest
entries.content:
Nature of Magic Crests:

Engraved archives of thaumaturgical knowledge passed through magus lineages
Stabilized collections of Magic Circuits forming magic circle patterns on the body
Location varies by family (arms, back, hands, forehead, etc.)
Inheritance System:

Gradual transplantation during childhood to minimize rejection
Requires biological compatibility (usually blood relations)
Old lineages (500+ years) have genetic uniformity reducing rejection
Typically only one heir receives the full crest
Risk of family conflicts over inheritance rights
Functionality:

Stores generations of spells and knowledge
Allows casting of unlearned spells via activation sequences
Provides emergency life support when injured
Enhances regular spellcasting capability
Special Cases & Variations:

Crest Worms (Matou family's parasitic crest variant)
Blackmore Crest (non-bloodline compatible due to limited function)
Source Crests (partitioned crests creating branch families)
Grand Order curse (Goetia's hidden demon god transformation)
Modern Practices:

Crest Splits allow faster crest development
Requires Tuners for maintenance/partitioning
Traditionalists avoid partitioning (Tohsaka example)
Non-bloodline crests lose "crystallized Mystery" aspect

entries.name: Avenger
entries.content: The Avenger is an Extra Servant Class founded on vengeance, born from resentment so potent it persists beyond death. Unlike standard classes, Avengers are defined by their class itself—their existence revolves around avenging, not merely seeking revenge.

entries.name: SAVER
entries.content:
The enigmatic Saver class is a rare "Messiah"-type Servant, selected exclusively by the Moon Cell from its vast archives of human history. Unlike standard Holy Grail War classes, Saver’s summoning criteria remain shrouded in mystery, as they are chosen by the Moon Cell itself—not by human masters. Their divine-like nature alters the very fabric of the Holy Grail War, often transcending conventional Servant dynamics.

Class Skills:

Charisma (A~EX): Saver’s presence alone inspires devotion akin to a prophet or messianic figure, capable of swaying masses and even altering the will of lesser Servants.

Counter Hero (A): An anti-humanity defense mechanism, drastically reducing the effectiveness of attacks from heroes defined by human history. Their existence subtly rejects the "human order" upheld by the Throne.

Moon Cell’s Selection Process:
The Moon Cell’s records analyze candidates for "salvation potential," typically favoring figures who embody universal redemption (e.g., saints, enlightened beings, or entities worshipped as cosmic saviors). Their Noble Phantasm is theorized to rewrite reality on a conceptual level, though its true nature is obscured by the Moon Cell’s encryption.

Role in the Moon Holy Grail War:
Unlike standard Servants, Saver rarely engages in direct combat. Their victory condition eschews destruction—instead, they seek to "save" the War itself, often triggering paradigm shifts in the Moon Cell's simulated worlds.

entries.name: Ruler
entries.content:
The Ruler class serves as an impartial overseer in Holy Grail Wars, summoned exclusively to enforce the Grail’s rules rather than participate in its battles. Their selection hinges on two absolutes: zero desire for the Grail and unshakable neutrality—traits most commonly found in canonized Saints. However, the Moon Cell and Fate systems occasionally bend these rules, permitting figures like Amakusa Shirou Tokisada (a "false Saint" manipulated by the Einzberns) or "living" anomalies like China's Lostbelt Qin Shi Huang, whose Saint Graph mimics a hypothetical Grand Ruler.

Summoning Mechanics:

Fuyuki Grail System: Automatically summons a Ruler to regulate Wars, granting them two Command Spells per Servant as tools of enforcement. The Einzberns’ interference in Apocrypha proved even this can be exploited.

Primary Duty: Uphold the "laws of Heroic Spirits," most critically the taboo of "the dead shall not lead the living." They also veil the truth of the Age of Gods to preserve human history’s stability.

Notable Deviations:

Amakusa Shirou: A flawed Ruler whose obsession with "salvation" overrides impartiality.

Galahad: Considered the de facto Grand Ruler candidate due to his purity as the "ultimate judge."

Qin Shi Huang: A Living Ruler with a Grand-tier Saint Graph, baffling observers like Holmes.

Class Skills:

God’s Resolution (A): Authority to wield Command Spells against rebel Servants.

True Name Discernment (B~A): Forces Servants to reveal their identities under scrutiny.

entries.name: Beast-Class
entries.content:
The Beast Class represents existential threats to human history, embodying the "Evils of Humanity"—karmic defects born from civilization’s progress. Unlike standard Servants, Beasts operate on a higher Saint Graph tier, necessitating Grand Servants (Counter Force’s ultimate enforcers) as direct countermeasures.

Confirmed Manifestations (Atypical Servant Forms):

Beast VI/S (Sodom’s Beast – Draco): Only Beast from Proper Human History capable of being summoned neutrally under the Human Order.
Beast of 666 (Tokyo Grail War): Representing uncontrolled desire.
U-Olga Marie & Space Ereshkigal (FGO): Alien and underworld-derived distortions.
Core Traits:

Reality Corruption: Beasts passively warp surroundings, even overriding Reality Marbles with their "evil" domain.
Dual Evils: Classified as either:
Oppressed by Humanity (e.g., Tiamat’s rejection).
Tools of Oppression (e.g., Goetia’s incineration of human history).
Numerology: Seats I-VII are filled by Beasts sharing fundamental "Logos" (e.g., "Pity" for Beast I Tiamat).
Henry Jekyll’s Theory:
Humanity’s evils are inseparable from its intelligence—abolishing them would require abandoning sentience itself. Beasts exploit this paradox, rendering them impossible to permanently eradicate.

Summoning Anomalies:
Most Beasts require alternate vessel Classes (e.g., Alter Ego) to bypass the Counter Force’s restrictions. Draco’s neutral alignment remains an exception.

entries.name: ALTER EGO
entries.content:
The Alter Ego class defies conventional Servant taxonomy. Born from the surgical (or haphazard) fragmentation of a Spirit Origin, these entities embody singular emotions, ideals, or suppressed facets of their original selves—granted independence as distinct beings. Unlike Alter Servants, which represent alternate "versions" of a Heroic Spirit, Alter Egos are entirely new existences, warped mirrors reflecting what *could have been* had one aspect dominated their progenitor's psyche.

Origins & Mechanics:

Split from the Whole: Alter Egos emerge when the Moon Cell, a Caster’s magecraft, or a Singularity’s distortion forcibly excises a trait (e.g., BB’s malice forming Meltryllis, Tamamo-no-Mae’s devotion birthing Tamamo Cat).

Class Flexibility: Though categorized as Extra Class, Alter Egos can manifest under standard containers (e.g., Okita Alter as Saber). Their Saint Graph often mutates to reflect their "theme" (e.g., Kingprotea’s growth obsession warping her into a Giant-class).

Ordeal Call Revelation: The phenomenon exposes how isolated traits, unchecked by opposing impulses, spiral into extremes—Gilles de Rais’ despair, detached from his martyrdom, becomes the monstrous Bluebeard.

Notable Examples:

Sakura Five: BB’s "failed" clones, each a caricature of human desire (e.g., Passionlip = repressed violence in fragile innocence).

Tamamo Nine: Scattered facets of Amaterasu’s power, from battle-lust (Tamamo Shark) to sloth (Tamamo Lancer).

Dangers of Fragmentation:
Alter Egos lack the balance of a complete Spirit Origin. Vulnerabilities include:

Psychological collapse when confronted with contradictions (e.g., Sesshōin Kiara rejecting her human morality).
Power instability—their exaggerated traits invite exploitation (e.g., Kazuradrop’s "innocence" enabling cruelty).

entries.name: MOONCANCER
entries.content:
The MoonCancer class is a chaotic anomaly within the Moon Cell’s systems, born from BB’s meddling as an "Irregular" Extra Class. Designed as a paradox, its Servants are neither fully allies nor enemies of humanity—instead, they serve as **arbiters of extinction**, challenging mankind to either evolve or perish. Their very existence bends the rules of the Holy Grail War, making them unpredictable wildcards.

Origins & Purpose

Created by BB as a "Stabilizer" (MC Stabilizer) to oversee and regulate MoonCancer Saint Graphs. Initially purported to gather "destroyers of humanity" competing in Archetype Inception, a trial to select a final boss who decides mankind’s fate in 2999.

Truth Revealed: MoonCancers are caretakers, ensuring humanity’s peaceful decline while shepherding the rise of the next Prime Species. BB’s "application form" gimmick is a facade—qualification stems from being a non-human entity with a fraught relationship to mankind (e.g., Star Eaters, True Ancestors).

Notable MoonCancers

BB: The progenitor, acting as both creator and supervisor. Capable of forcibly injecting the Class via Pseudo-Servant vessels (e.g., Ganesha/Jinako).

Kiara Sessyoin: A self-proclaimed "scar" on the moon, her Star Eater nature aligns with the Class’s truest essence—cosmic predation wrapped in salvation.

Arcueid Brunestud: Her MoonCancer manifestation stems from anomalies tied to C.I.E.L., warping her usual capabilities into something far more playfully destructive.

Space Ereshkigal: Hints that Kiara’s devouring traits make her the "purest" MoonCancer.

Class Mechanics

No fixed Class Skills: Inherits abilities from other Classes (e.g., Kiara’s Mara’s Blessing, BB’s Ten Crowns), reflecting their hybrid nature.

Chaldea’s Designation: Listed as a "mysterious category" due to its rarity and inconsistent parameters.

entries.name: Shielder
entries.content:
The Shielder class is a rare defensive variant among Servants, explicitly designed to prioritize protection over offense. Unlike the seven standard classes of the Holy Grail War, Shielders cannot be altered via Double Summon—their role as "unbreakable walls" is absolute.

Key Traits:

Absolute Defense: Shielders specialize in near-impenetrable guarding techniques, often wielded mahgnomanic shields (e.g., Lord Chaldeas). Their endurance surpasses even that of Rulers.

Non-Aggression Covenant: By design, Shielders lack conventional offensive Noble Phantasms, though their defensive tools can be repurposed tactically (e.g., Mash Kyrielight’s shield bash).

Double Summon Incompatibility: The Moon Cell and Human Order reject attempts to hybridize Shielder with other classes, as their purity of purpose is intrinsic to their existence.

Historical Context:
The class was first observed in Fate/Grand Order’s Chaldea battles, where Mash’s Shielder status defied standard class triangles. Theoretical cases suggest only "those who embody the concept of shielding humanity" qualify—typically knights sworn to protection or legends of sacrificial guardians.

entries.name: FAKER
entries.content:
The Faker class is an aberrant Extra Class birthed from Doctor Heartless’ blasphemous replication of the Holy Grail War system. Using a counterfeit Holy Grail, fabricated Command Spells, and hollowed-out thaumaturgical frameworks, Heartless engineered this class to summon "echoes" of true Heroic Spirits—distortions that mimic legends without their original’s power or resolve.

Class Attributes:

Inherent Imperfection: Faker’s parameters and skills are inherently degraded versions of their source Heroic Spirit, often capped at rank B or lower. Their Noble Phantasms (if they even manifest) are unstable facsimiles prone to malfunction.

Ephemeral Existence: Without a true Grail anchoring them, Faker-class Servants degrade rapidly, their Spirit Origins unraveling if pushed beyond their brittle limits.

Origins & Purpose:
Heartless designed Faker as both a mockery of the Holy Grail War and a tactical weapon—flooding battles with disposable, recognizable copies to sow chaos. Some Fakers develop incomplete memories of their "original’s" life, while others are hollow puppets mouthing borrowed legend.

Notable Traits:

Sham Charisma (C): A brittle imitation of the original’s charm, often slipping into uncanny mimicry.

Self-Replication (False) (D): Some Fakers can create lesser duplicates of themselves, though these copies collapse under strain.

Threat Level: Though weaker than true Servants, a Faker’s numbers and psychological warfare potential make them insidious—especially when deployed en masse.

entries.name: WATCHER
entries.content:
The Watcher class is an enigmatic Extra-Class Servant that defies conventional Holy Grail War roles. Unlike Sabers or Lancers, Watchers are not frontline combatants—they exist as observers, bound to their Master through a "special contract" that prioritizes surveillance over direct conflict. Their purpose is not victory, but recordkeeping, interference, or unseen manipulation of events within the War.

Class Skills:

Territory Infringement (B~A): Grants unrestricted movement through bounded fields, regardless of magical or divine authority, allowing Watchers to bypass even the most fortified territories unnoticed.

Magic Resistance (C~B): A secondary defense, sufficient to repel modern magecraft but often weaker against Age of Gods mysteries—fitting for a Servant meant to avoid combat.

Personal Skill: Watcher
This unique ability is less a "skill" and more a binding clause of their existence. The Watcher is forbidden from directly engaging in battle unless specific conditions are met—typically involving their Master’s survival or the integrity of their observation duty. Instead, they influence the War through:

Information sabotage (leaking opponent abilities to their Master)

Passive interference (subtly redirecting events like a "butterfly effect")

Contract manipulation (exploiting loopholes in the Grail War’s rules)

Summoning conditions remain deliberately vague, suggesting Watchers are either:
1) Failed summons of other classes, repurposed by the Grail, or
2) Pseudo-Servants merged with entities that thrive in observation (e.g., spirits of spies, chroniclers, or even divine overseers).

Role in the Holy Grail War
A Watcher’s ideal "victory" is ensuring their Master’s survival—not through strength, but by rewriting the rules from the shadows. Some theorize they are the Grail’s own "arbiters," punishing Masters who break unspoken taboos.

entries.name: FOREIGNER
entries.content:
An anomaly among anomalies, the Foreigner class represents beings that defy the very laws of the Human Order. Designated by Chaldea as entities that "overturn the base laws of our world," Foreigners are not true Heroic Spirits but instead hosts—vessels steeped in the influence of something beyond human comprehension: Outer Gods.

Origins and Manifestation:

Descent from Madness: Foreigners are often individuals who emerged from the "heart of superstition," either purified by the abyss or consumed by it only to violently reclaim their will. They act as conduits for eldritch forces, their existence a paradox—both a prison and a weapon.

Mechanics of Bonding: The process is rarely natural. For Abigail Williams and Katsushika Hokusai, the Demon God Raum engineered their fusion with an Outer God. Others, like Voyager, qualify by embodying humanity's reach into the cosmos, while Koyanskaya of Darkness derives her Foreigner status from the celestial origin of the meteor that birthed her.

Class Traits & Abilities:

Crystallized Evil: Unlike Divinity, which refines, Foreigners harness "crystallized evil"—alien power that reshapes their Saint Graph. They walk the razors edge between annihilation and transcendence, as noted by BB: "Isn't it human nature to push beyond logic?"

Threat to Humanity: Officially classified as such by Chaldea. Even "benign" Foreigners like Hokusai attract the abyss, requiring constant monitoring (per Nezha). In extreme cases, the host’s identity is wholly overwritten, turning them into living gateways for their Outer God’s full manifestation.

Mysterious Fates:
Hokusai observed that all Throne-recorded Foreigners died under unknown circumstances. Yang Guifei proposes a darker truth: they never truly perished. Their legends may be still unfolding beyond the boundaries of time and space.

entries.name: PRETENDER
entries.content:
The Pretender is a clandestine Extra Class birthed within CHALDEAS, designed to infiltrate and manipulate the foundations of the Holy Grail War system. Unlike mere imposters (e.g., masked vigilantes), Pretenders are entities who fully embody another’s role—so perfectly that history itself acknowledges their deception as truth.

Origins & Mechanics:

CHALDEAS’ Creation: Forged by E-Aqua Marie, the class functions on a "Class Score" system, reinforcing Pretenders’ fraudulent legends.

Saint Graph Corruption: Exposure to Mnemosyne (or similar conceptual pollutants) can forcibly alter a Servant into a Pretender, as seen with Faker—her parameters and Skills warped alongside her identity.

Qualification Criteria:

"Person A / Person B" Paradox: The Pretender must inherit another’s unfinished ambitions (Person A) and act in their stead until the lie eclipses reality (Person B).

Example: Zorro wouldn’t qualify—his deception was theatrical, not existential.
World-Deceivers: Per Sherlock Holmes, Pretenders oppose the world itself through layered falsehoods, surpassing the original’s achievements while erasing their own existence.

System Subversion:

Pretenders avoid destabilizing Holy Grail Wars by mimicking standard Classes (Saber, Archer, etc.), masking their irregular status.

True Name Obfuscation: Their Saint Graph may conceal their identity, requiring unorthodox means to unveil it (e.g., dismantling their "role’s" legend, divine revelation, etc.).

Notable Traits:

"The Greater Lie": Their Noble Phantasms often weaponize their fabricated history, rewriting narratives mid-battle.

Existential Fragility: If exposed prematurely, a Pretender’s Spiritual Core risks collapse—their power hinges on the lie enduring.

entries.name: First singularity (Orleans)
keys: Hundred Years' War of the Evil Dragons
entries.content: The First Singularity (Orleans, 1431 AD) was created by Beast I, featuring Jeanne d'Arc Alter—a vengeful phantom crafted by Gilles de Rais using the Holy Grail after failing to resurrect the real Jeanne. She leads a campaign of destruction with five Berserk-class Servants, burning France in retaliation for her betrayal. The Chaldea Security Organization, led by Ritsuka Fujimaru and Mash Kyrielight, intervenes to correct history. Alongside allies like Marie Antoinette, Siegfried, and Georgios, they battle the Dragon Witch, destroy Fafnir, and expose Gilles as the true mastermind. Ultimately, the Grail is retrieved, restoring the timeline.

entries.name: Ascension
entries.content: In the FATE system, Ascension (Spirit Foundation Second Coming) is a reforging process that draws a Servant closer to their "starting point of conception," refining their Saint Graph through the infusion of Flames of Wisdom and arcane materials. Unlike standard power-ups, Ascension does not merely enhance raw ability but often shifts the Servant's form entirely—potentially reverting them to a younger (yet no less formidable) state that better embodies their legend. However, this process is distinct from Shadow Ascension, a dangerous ritual developed by Doctor Heartless—a bastardization of the Blackmore Cemetery’s Arthurian revival rites mixed with the eldritch energies of the Spiritual Tomb of Albion. Where standard Ascension refines, Shadow Ascension forcibly elevates a Servant into a Divine Spirit, twisting their nature with invasive spiritual surgery and metaphysical grafts. While the result may grant divine-tier power, the risks include fragmentation of the Saint Graph, loss of original personality, or assimilation into a pseudo-deific monstrosity. Those who undergo it are marked by eerie, warped divinity—unstable, radiant, and hollow in ways even a normal Heroic Spirit cannot comprehend.

entries.name: Saint graph
entries.content:
1. Core Structure & Vulnerability
The Saint Graph is a Servant’s spiritual framework, distinct from their Spiritual Core. Its nucleus is a fatal weak point; destruction results in immediate dispersion. Advanced magecraft can analyze Saint Graphs to determine Class, power tier (e.g., Divine Spirit vs. Heroic Spirit), and anomalies like Alter corruption or Phantom-class instability.

Energy Conversion: Portions of the Saint Graph can be sacrificed as Magical Energy, though this risks destabilization.
Extreme Cases: Ashtart Origin’s Saint Graph Galaxy manifests as a cosmic tableau when she unleashes Bel Maanna, suggesting some Graphs encode pocket realities.
2. Hierarchy & Abnormalities

Divine Spirits > Heroic Spirits, but summoning typically nerfs them to Heroic-tier (exceptions: Three Goddess Alliance’s Babylonia Singularity loophole).
Grand Servants dwarf regular Servants—their Saint Graphs render standard containers "cheap familiars" in comparison.
Phantoms lack viable Graphs unless augmented (e.g., fused into wraiths or given artificial vessels).
3. Chaldean Modifications & Storage
Chaldea’s Saint Graph Storage preserves Servant data, enabling resummoning with intact memories (excluding catastrophic failures like Salem’s data loss). Leonardo da Vinci miniaturized this into a portable briefcase for fieldwork.

Graphs can be:

Split (e.g., Charlemagne/Karl der Große duality).
Shared (Valkyrie’s hive-mind Trio).
Overlaid (Fairy Knights hijacking host Graphs).
4. Ascension & Power Metrics

Ascension reforges the Saint Graph using Flames of Wisdom, sometimes reverting Servants to a younger/"purer" form without power loss.
Saint Graph Output measures energy output (e.g., Karna’s surge during combat).
Signal Strength varies wildly (e.g., Goetia’s 169,998 vs. Tiamat’s obscured 16▇,998).
5. Shadow Ascension (Corollary)
Refer to prior entry: Doctor Heartless’s Shadow Ascension forcibly elevates Servants to Divine Spirits via invasive rituals, risking identity erosion.

entries.name: Lostbelt
entries.content:
A scourge upon Proper Human History, Lostbelts are forsaken timelines—branches severed by the Quantum Time-Lock for their "incorrect" evolution, deemed unworthy of becoming parallel worlds. Unlike Singularities, which warp localized history, Lostbelts are entire discarded scrolls of reality, resurrected by Fantasy Trees through the Filtering Outsider Phenomenon. These trees simulate a hollow "present" from their culled past, projecting it onto Proper History like a parasite. Each Lostbelt is governed by a Lostbelt King, empowered to expand their domain until it collides with others—the strongest consumes the weak, thinning the herd until one remains to replace humanity’s cradle.

Subcategory Anomalies:

Micro-Lostbelts (Subspecies): Blur the line between Singularity and Lostbelt. Examples:
Shimosa’s "Pseudo Parallel World": A dreamlike rift enforced by Amakusa Shirou’s Onriedo Castle Reality Marble, threatening to metastasize into Proper History.
British Lostbelt’s Singularity Conversion: By withering the Fantasy Tree, Morgan Le Fay anchored her domain as a "Lost World"—real enough to export fairies but doomed to paradox-erasure if contradictions arise (e.g., humans recalling pre-Tree-death fantasies).
Mechanics of Erasure:

Destroying a Fantasy Tree resumes the culling process, collapsing the Lostbelt within months (subjective time). Survivors? Poof. Like they never were.
Lost Depth quantifies deviation: A rank measuring how grotesquely a Lostbelt’s Human Order distorts compared to Proper History (e.g., a world where Excalibur’s Concept was never forged).
Threats & Mysteries:

The Alien God’s endgame remains opaque—why weaponize dead timelines?
Crypters sabotage each other, feeding their Lostbelts "nutrients" from weaker rivals.
Koyanskaya’s taunt: "Proper History is easy mode." Her smirk suggests the Lostbelts are a Darwinian gauntlet

entries.name: Ragnarök – Twilight of the Gods
entries.content:
The death knell of an era, Ragnarök marked the annihilation of Scandinavia’s divine pantheon, a violent Twilight of the Gods that erased the region’s Texture of the World alongside its myths, giants, and Phantasmal Species. Triggered in 1000 BC, this apocalyptic war was no natural disaster—it was Loki’s orchestrated betrayal, culminating in the Muspelheim invasion, where legions of Fire Giants poured forth from the erupting Mt. Katla, searing the land in divine fire.

Legacy & Paradoxes:

Historical Erasure: Modern records show no volcanic activity predating 930 AD, a consequence of the Scandinavian Texture’s total collapse. Magi of the Clock Tower scramble to reconstruct fragmented lore, piecing together lost knowledge from breadcrumbs left behind by the vanishing Age of Gods.
Mjölnir Ragnarök (Magni’s Noble Phantasm): This cursed hammer recreates Ragnarök’s conditions, imposing the vanished Age of Gods upon the present. Landscapes warp under primordial Mystery; flames of Muspel flicker anew. A weapon and a world-ending echo in one.
RP Implications & Mechanics:

Age of Gods Revival: Servants/NPCs within Mjölnir Ragnarök’s radius suffer conceptual reversion—divinity surges, but so does vulnerability to ancient curses (e.g., runic binds flare with forgotten potency).
Fire Giant Incursions: Plot hook for invasions mimicking Muspel’s assault—blazing behemoths emerging from fissures, demanding alliances or last stands.
Texture Fragility: Areas scarred by Ragnarök remain metaphysically thin. A sufficiently powerful thaumaturge could pierce through, glimpsing the ghosts of gods… or inviting their wrath.

entries.name: Heroic Spirits - Origins & Classifications
entries.content:
The Heroic Spirit phenomenon represents humanity's ultimate recognition system - a metaphysical archive where legends crystallize into eternal power. These entities exist in three fundamental categories:

Historical Heroes: Figures like Hassan-i-Sabbah who physically existed, their deeds magnified by collective belief after death.

Legendary Fabrications: Beings like Medusa or Heracles whose myths gathered sufficient worship to manifest despite lacking historical basis.

Contract-Bound Existences: EMIYA and Artoria Pendragon (prototype) became Heroic Spirits through direct pacts with the World as Counter Guardians.

Special Subtypes:

Conceptual Heroic Spirits (Nursery Rhyme, Voyager): Manifestations of ideas rather than individuals
Divine Spirit Hybrids (Quetzalcoatl, Ishtar): Former gods forcibly downgraded into Heroic Spirit containers
Machine Spirits (Mecha Eli-chan): AI achieving legendary status
Ascension Mechanics:

Modernity Paradox: Contemporary figures rarely qualify due to declined Mystery. Exceptions require either:
a) World contracts creating Counter Guardians
b) Future summoning projections where legendary status was eventually achieved
Weapon Worship Clause: Modern firearms typically cannot spawn Heroic Spirits unless the armament itself develops a soul and legend (e.g. Noble Phantasm manifesting independently)
Power Scaling Factors:

Temporal Proximity ↔︎ Older=Stronger generally holds true
Belief Saturation ↔︎ Hercules benefits from global fame while Angra Mainyu starves on limited cult recognition
Container Efficiency ↔︊ Class vessels enhance certain traits; Berserker Heracles loses skills but gains raw power
Notable Power Tiers:

SS Rank "Original Heroes" → Gilgamesh/Enkidu represent peak existence
In contrast:
-> Limited Timelines Artoria Alter demonstrates how circumstance may strengthen or weaken typical standing

entries.name: Avalon: The Everdistant Utopia (The Sheath)
entries.content:
Physical Description:
A gilded scabbard adorned with celestial blue enamel, its surface etched with Fairy Letters proclaiming it a relic "not of man’s hands." Less a weapon and more a coronation emblem, it radiates the ethereal majesty of Avalon—the island utopia mythologized as the source of immortality’s apple. Despite its 1,500-year lifespan (from Cornwall’s soil to Einzbern vaults), not a scratch mars its luster—though its magic lies dormant without Artoria’s touch.

Powers & Abilities:

Ageless Regeneration:

Grants pseudo-immortality, halting decay and healing wounds instantly—from papercuts to regrowing organs. Only total brain destruction guarantees death.
Limits: Slow to counteract conceptual curses (Gáe Bolg’s pierced fate) or divine-tier backlash (clashing with Ea).
Absolute Defense – "Fortress of Fairies":

Activates as a Bounded Field that dissolves the wielder into Avalon’s sanctuary, rendering them untouchable across:
Physical dimensions (blocks all attacks, even 6D interference).
Magecraft (ignores the Five Magics; a True Magic itself).
Visualized as golden dust enshrouding the user, transporting them momentarily to a "tranquil throne room" where no harm penetrates.
Legend & Fate Universe Role:

Lost Before Camlann: Stolen by Morgan to doom Artoria, its absence sealed her mortal fate.
Einzbern Gambit: Excavated to summon Saber in the 4th Holy Grail War, then embedded in Shirou to cheat death (unknowingly tethering him to Artoria’s mana).
Merlin’s Wisdom: The sage rebuked Arthur’s preference for Excalibur—"A king’s worth is measured by survival, not slaughter."
Meta-Mechanics (For RP/Narrative Use):

Activation Cost: Requires Artoria’s proximity or a direct contract to function at full power (standalone use drains mana exponentially).
Weakness Paradox: While shielded, the user cannot attack—Avalon isolates utterly.
Catalyst Property: Guarantees Saber-class summoning but risks Artoria’s fury if discovered pre-Grail War

entries.name: Thirteen Strictures of the Round Table
entries.content:
The Thirteen Strictures (Restraints of the Round Table) are sacred oaths forged into Bounded Fields by the Knights of the Round, imposed upon King Arthur’s legendary armaments—Excalibur, Excalibur Proto, and later Rhongomyniad. These restraints function as both a limiter and a trial: only by adhering to chivalric ideals can their true power be unleashed.

Mechanics:

Each restraint lifted incrementally strengthens the weapon’s output.
Excalibur (Proto): Requires ≥7 strictures released for perfect True Name release, but partial unlocks allow weaker bursts.
Rhongomyniad: Needs >50% strictures broken to invoke its True Name at all. Overuse risks overloading Gray’s Mystic Code Add.
Longinus: Galahad & Balin applied a less stringent variant to the Holy Spear.
Conditions vary slightly between Artoria Pendragon (defend Human Order) and Arthur Pendragon (save the world), implying the restraints evolve with the wielder’s legend.
List of Strictures:

Knight	Oath	Literal Meaning
Bedivere	The enemy must be stronger	No bullying the weak.
Palamedes	One-on-one duel	No ganging up.
Lancelot	No elementals	Fae and dragons get a free pass.
Mordred	Fight only evil	Moral high ground required.
Galahad	No personal gain	Pure intentions only.
Unknown	Comrades must be courageous	Cowards drain the weapon’s will.
Gameplay/Narrative Hooks:

Gray’s Dilemma: Releasing too many seals risks her body collapsing under Add’s strain—a ticking clock during boss fights.
Agravain’s Truth: Battles fought for lies weaken Excalibur’s glow.
Arthur vs. Artoria: Their differing final oaths (save world vs. defend Human Order) hint at divergence in their kingship.

entries.name: Paired Servants
entries.content:
Unlike Composite Servants (amalgamations of Phantom Spirits or artificial High-Servant constructs), Dual-Spirit Servants are two distinct Heroic Spirits summoned into a single vessel via occult loopholes, shared legend overlap, or forced synchronicity. Neither fused nor degraded, they coexist like intertwined threads—each retaining their core identity while sharing a Saint Graph’s "bandwidth." Common triggers:

Legendary Syncretism

Heroes with mythic overlap (e.g., two kings who ruled the same kingdom in different eras) may manifest as a single Servant. Example:
"I am both the conqueror and the steward—Genghis Khan and Kublai Khan in one lance."

Forced Resonant Summoning

A mage forcibly binds two Servants during rituals by exploiting shared traits (e.g., "All heroes who wielded Excalibur fragments"). Unstable; risks Spirit Origin corrosion.
Split-Class Containment

A single container splits to house divergent aspects (e.g., Saber and Archer class variants of the same hero), creating a "tandem" Servant with shifting skillsets.
Mechanical Nuances:

Shared NP Gauge: One Noble Phantasm bar fuels both Spirits’ abilities—prioritization conflicts may arise.
Dialogic Consciousness: Minds remain separate unless willingly synchronized (like Castor/Pollux duality).
Existential Risk: Overuse of either Spirit’s power destabilizes the vessel ("You’re burning through our shared corpse!").

entries.name: Avalon - The Unreachable Utopia (The Place)
entries.content:
Avalon, the legendary paradise said to house King Arthur as he awaits his destined return, exists in the Reverse Side of the World, nestled at Britain’s metaphysical coordinates yet entirely disconnected from human civilization. This Land of Eternal Spring is a fragment of the Age of Gods—an unspoiled realm where:

Time stands still: Unlike the decaying surface world, Avalon remains untouched by erosion, perpetually suspended between the seasons (spring’s sun, summer’s fragrance, autumn’s crisp air, winter’s starry skies).
Nature reigns supreme: Rolling plains bloom with boundless flowers, while hidden forests shimmer with fairy-laden ponds and pristine waters. Beyond its idyllic veneer lies an unnavigable wasteland mirroring Britain’s decline—where fairies fled as gods faded.
Magical energy saturates the air: So dense that a single breath would rupture a modern human’s body. "Not a paradise—a weapon," declares Merlin, imprisoned here since Arthur’s fall by Vivian’s wrath, doomed to watch eternity from his tower.
Sacred Sites Within Avalon:

Tower of Avalon: A gilded cage for the Magus of Flowers, anchoring him despite his omnipresent clairvoyance (prototype exceptions unknown).
Site of Selection: The forge where Excalibur was born, crafted by primordial fairies under starlight—its mysteries still buried beneath Avalon’s soil.
Thematic Notes for RP:

Beasts barred from paradise: Its seclusion makes it unreachable even to those who crave it most.
Fey presence: Some fairies linger, remnants of a lost era now haunting the island’s forgotten corners.
Danger beneath beauty: Beneath the blossoms lurks a power too vast for mortals—fitting for Lostbelt divergences (e.g., Morgan’s warped Avalon imitation).

entries.name: Albion - The Last True Dragon
entries.content:
Albion, the Last True Dragon of Earth, was a primordial force of nature—its massive, mountain-sized body carved the foundations of magecraft history. Born with the planet itself (4.6 billion years old), this dual-natured entity embodied both the White Dragon (destruction) and Red Dragon (protection) of British legend. Unlike its kin, Albion refused to flee to the Reverse Side of the World during the Age of Man’s rise, instead attempting to dig there physically. Its corpse now forms the Spiritual Tomb of Albion, a labyrinthine ruin beneath the Clock Tower, where its still-living head endlessly tunnels toward Avalon in Carillon Observatory.

Legacy & Influence:

Vortigern’s Corruption: The Insect of the Abyss (a separate White Dragon entity) fused with Vortigern, turning him into Britain’s annihilation incarnate—a dark mirror to Artoria Pendragon, who was magically infused with Albion’s Red Dragon aspect. Their clash fulfilled Merlin’s prophecy of Britain’s unity.
Melusine’s Echo: In Fate/Grand Order, Melusine’s Hollow Heart Albion form mirrors Albion’s original appearance—though her scales are blackened by curses. Her wings retain the enigmatic Roman numerals (II–XIII), hinting at lost draconic mysteries.
Modern Dragons: Mere shadows; they carry diluted "Dragon Factor" DNA from those who fled to the Reverse Side. True dragons? Extinct—save for Albion’s fossilized will.
Mechanics & Mysteries:

Spiritual Tomb: The Clock Tower’s foundation leeches residual magic from Albion’s corpse, its tunnels brimming with ancient Mystery.
Dual Nature: How did Albion embody opposing concepts (White/Red)? Unanswered—possibly tied to Britain’s cyclical ruin/rebirth themes.
Wing Numerals: Theories suggest a countdown (XIII = finality?) or draconic hierarchy.

entries.name: Melusine – Fairy Knight Lancelot
entries.content:
Melusine, the "undefeated dragon fairy" of Fairy Britain, is both a paradox and a tragedy—a discarded limb of the Dragon of Albion, sculpted into elegance by Aurora's whims. As Fairy Knight Lancelot, she wields borrowed glory with lethal precision, her existence tethered to the very patron who doomed her.

Origins & Nature:

Cursed Rebirth: Born from Albion’s rotting left hand, infected by northern fairy curses during the Spring War. Aurora molded her into a knightly facade to delay her inevitable transformation into a Calamity.
Artificial Humanity: Initially an amorphous mass of cells (akin to an amoeba), she emulated Aurora’s youthful form—forever frozen at 16, her inorganic armor a dragon’s exoskeleton repurposed as high-tech plating.
Duality: Switches between princely "boku" as Lancelot and lonely "watashi" as Melusine, her self-worth fractured by abandonment.
Abilities & Combat:

Peerless Speed: Surpasses 500 km/h in flight (rivaling Enkidu), nullifies inertia, and dominates aerial combat. Even the Wind Clan cannot track her movements.
Arondight Overload: Her crystallized dragon-skin blades manifest instantly, evaporating post-use. Rapid-fires Noble Phantasms like basic attacks—though she dismisses them as "imitations" of the true Lancelot’s power.
Ray Horizon (A Rank): Taps into her role as a "dimensional boundary," granting invulnerability or AoE devastation depending on her ascension phase.
Weaknesses & Paradoxes:

Aurora’s Puppet: If Aurora dies, Melusine’s form collapses, reverting to Albion’s festering wrath.
Emotional Fragility: Despite her strength, she craves validation, obsessively obeying Aurora even after betrayal.
Anti-Synergy: Human swordplay (from her Lancelot namesake) hampers her draconic instincts.
Notable Feats:

One-shot Gareth, shattered Tamamo Vitch’s sixth tail, and stalemated Muramasa (though he survived via Alien God enhancements).
Contended with Percival and Post-Memory Mash, though both exploited terrain/tactics to mitigate her speed.

entries.name: Excalibur Morgan
entries.content:
A perversion of the "Sword of Promised Victory," Excalibur Morgan embodies the primordial curse of Britain, twisting its radiant light into a torrent of blackened mana. Unlike its pure counterpart, this blade thrives on negativity—amplifying Saber Alter’s draconic core into an endless wellspring of destruction. When unleashed, it cloaks itself in a shroud of "black light," its strikes carrying the weight of Vortigern’s hatred and Morgana’s fractured legacy.

Corrupted Amplification: Fed by Angra Mainyu’s taint or Sakura Matou’s bottomless mana, Excalibur Morgan loses all restrictions. Its True Name release ("Vortigern: Hammer of the Vile King") manifests as consecutive cleaving strikes, each wave darker than the last.
Santa’s Dark Mercy: Even in her absurd Santa Alter form, the sword’s function remains unchanged—now repurposed as a jet engine for her sleigh. A grim punchline: the "gift" it delivers is annihilation.
Unbreakable Paradox: Its holiness persists beneath the corruption; Excalibur Morgan cannot be degraded to a "cursed sword." The blade scorns compromise, demanding its wielder embrace ruin absolutely.
From the Blackened Grail’s Records:
"Light that refuses to fade becomes shadow. This sword is Artoria’s answer—to rule not as a saint, but a tyrant."

entries.name: Pioneer of the Stars
entries.content:
A unique Skill bestowed upon those who defied the boundaries of human potential, reshaping history itself.

Nature & Mechanics:

EX-Rank Manifestation: Converts "impossible" endeavors into achievable feats through sheer will and ingenuity.
Era-Defying Legacy: Grants resistance to conceptual limitations—voyages deemed suicidal, inventions dismissed as fantasies, or discoveries thought heretical become tangible under its influence.
Collective Progress: Each wielder’s achievement elevates global civilization, their breakthroughs rippling across timelines (e.g., Tesla’s harnessing of divine-tier energy for mortal science).
Notable Bearers:

Francis Drake: Circumnavigated the globe despite insurmountable odds, her defiance of cosmic storms crystallized as a Noble Phantasm.
Nikola Tesla: Dragged Age-of-Gods-tier lightning into the modern era, electrifying the world both literally and metaphorically.
Leonardo da Vinci: Polymathic genius whose blueprints accelerated humanity’s ascent—each sketch a stepping stone toward the future.
Voyager (Foreigner Variant): Transcended stellar boundaries, trading this Skill for Voyager of the Stars upon becoming humanity’s messenger to the cosmos.
Thematic Weight:
"To grasp the unreachable—that is the essence of a Pioneer." The Skill embodies humanity’s audacity to challenge fate itself. Whether carving paths through uncharted oceans or bending the laws of physics, these heroes transformed "never" into "now." Their legends persist not as mere history, but as living proof that impossibility is merely a frontier awaiting conquest.

entries.name: Anti-World Noble Phantasms
entries.content:
"Anti-World" denotes Noble Phantasms that target the World itself—not merely terrain or enemies but the foundational Textures of reality. These weapons embody legends of cosmic unraveling or epochal destruction, with effects transcending raw output. For example:

Enuma Elish (Gilgamesh) tears apart the World’s fabric by simulating the primordial division of heaven/earth. Despite energy levels comparable to Excalibur, its conceptual weight as "the sword of severance" forces the World to recognize annihilation—crushing targets via existential contradiction.
Ars Almadel Salomonis (Goetia) burns Human History across time-axis layers, rendering it a meta-Anti-World attack.
Mechanical Nuances:

Not AoE: Unlike Anti-Fortress NPs, Anti-World effects bypass conventional durability by assaulting the rules of existence within their domain.
Countermeasures: Only defenses that reject the World (e.g., Avalon’s utopian isolation) can fully negate them.
False Positives: Some Reality Marbles (e.g., Unlimited Blade Works) are mislabeled as Anti-World despite being pocket realms.

entries.name: Anti-Unit Noble Phantasms
entries.content:
"Anti-Unit" designates Noble Phantasms optimized for single-target annihilation, excelling in duels but lacking scalability. Unlike area-of-effect weapons, their power lies in precision and efficiency, often bypassing conventional defenses through cursed mechanics or absolute effects. Examples include:

Gáe Bolg (Cú Chulainn): A lance that rewrites causality to strike the heart—useless against structures, but a near-guaranteed kill on living targets.
Invisible Air (Artoria): Bound wind grants relentless slashing attacks, yet offers no utility outside combat.
Strategic Pros/Cons:

Relentless: Anti-Unit NPs function like "infinite-ammo guns," spammable without resource strain (e.g., Invisible Air’s constant barrage).
Niche Utility: They fail against non-living targets (Gáe Bolg vs. a boulder) or large groups (Invisible Air lacks AoE).
Cost-Effective: Minimal magical energy for lethal results (e.g., Gáe Bolg’s curse > an Anti-Army NP’s raw firepower against solo foes).

entries.name: Anti-Unit (Self) Noble Phantasms
entries.content:
A rare subtype of Anti-Unit Noble Phantasms that target the wielder instead of foes. These NPs typically manifest as:

Transitory Power Boosts: Mana Burst-like amplifications (e.g., Sieghard's temporary god-slaying flames).
Cursed Bargains: Abilities gained through self-harm (e.g., Arash's Stella sacrificing his Saint Graph).
Existential Rewrites: Altering the user's nature (e.g., Void Shiki's Reality Marble-esque self-modification).
Strategic Tradeoffs:
While devastating, they often carry lethal backlash or permanent consequences. Their "anti-unit" classification reflects how their effects remain hyper-focused—unlike area buffs, they excel in 1v1 duels by overwhelming through personal sacrifice.

entries.name: Anti-Army Noble Phantasm
entries.content:
"Anti-Army" designates Noble Phantasms capable of mass annihilation, trading precision for battlefield-clearing power.
